_about: F51 economy sim (scripts/bots/economy.mjs + career.ts): bots play whole careers, rank 0 → the final shift, on the real engine + the real content files, buying upgrades between shifts. Measuring only: nothing here changes the game. Bot skills are the F27 bots (bots.json). Same seeds = the same numbers.
_careers: careerSeeds = how many careers per bot skill × buy style (seeds 1…n). maxShifts = a career stops here if it never gets to win the final shift. finalTries = how many times a career plays the final shift (it keeps going after a loss, as the game does: One Of Us, try again) before it stops.
_buyStyles: How a bot shops between shifts (all its scraps, every time the shop is open). spread = one level at a time into whatever has the fewest levels (older first on a tie) · rush = the newest open band first, spread inside it, then the band before · activesFirst = actives (and the extra active slots) first, then spread. neverBuy = upgrades no bot buys (empty since 2026-10-29 — Muzzy: why not?; Dense Goop's faster pieces measured +2–3 s, it can help). bands = the rank each upgrade band starts at (design/progression.md).
_activePriority: Which owned actives a bot takes into the shift when it has more than slots (first = most wanted).
_console: Console stand-ins (as the final-shift bots, runFinal.ts): a broken machine sends the bot to the console after its reaction time; each repair takes bots.json consoleRepairSec × (its steps ÷ the steps it has with no upgrades), so Quick Fix and the max-level fixes save time there. The shift runs at breakdowns.json consoleTimeScale × Focus Mode meanwhile. A swap is a hold of src/input/controls.ts swapHoldMs (Goop Swap makes it shorter): the bot waits through it. Ready actives are fired after the bot's reaction time.
_effects: Upgrade effect runs: each upgrade at the rank it opens and again at effectLateRanks (45 = late game: every twist, the white goop · 50 = the final shift), its level 1 and its max level vs owning nothing, the same seeds both ways. A slot upgrade is measured with one more active owned (slotTestActives, in order) than fits without it. effectSeeds = seeds per bot per rank.
_effectCompanions: Upgrades that only work through an active are measured with that active owned + equipped in BOTH runs (Sealing Bonus only adds charge to actives).
_fireWhen: When the bots fire a ready active. pieceMatchesCrack = only while the falling piece is the colour of an open crack (the way a player feeds a crack with Colorizer's pieces); openCrack = while any crack is open and not plugged (F75: Goop Dump's rain is wild — it plugs any); missing = as soon as it's ready (after the bot's reaction time). A first run fired everything at once: Colorizer then measured as harmful.
_feel: feelThreshold = the PLACEHOLDER change we call 'big enough to feel' until Muzzy calibrates it by playing with and without an upgrade (Ask Muzzy, SPRINT 24 Notes): seconds survived, win rate (share of shifts that meet the quota) and the quota (share of the cracks needed that got sealed). An upgrade below all three for every bot is listed as 'no measurable effect'. feltDirectly = upgrades you feel in your hands (speed, a hold), not in outcomes: listed apart, not judged by these numbers.
_final: The final shift with a real career's upgrades: each career's loadout on the day it reached rank 50, finalSeeds shifts each (seeds 1…n), plus the same seeds with no upgrades. finalLeaveOut = actives the bots take OFF for the final shift (a first sim run: Goop Dump's rain of one-colour goop drowned every final shift, 0 of 10 won — a player would learn to leave it home); the results page also shows the loadout with them still on.
_finalTakeBack: Passives a smart player takes back (free) before the final shift, spending the scraps elsewhere — Muzzy 2026-10-29: Dense Goop's faster pieces cost the Sharp bot most of its final-shift wins (F51 re-run).
_quick: npm run sim:economy -- --quick (check:full): careers cut at quickToRank, 1 seed, a few effect runs, a few final shifts — it only proves the sim runs and repeats; the full run's numbers are the ones to read.
